We're implementing Story 7.3 "Empty-Period Handling" in a Flutter app called Cerne (reflective journaling app, Clean Architecture, repo root /Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b). This is the final story in Epic 7 (export feature). Stories 7.1 and 7.2 are already done: 7.1 built the export-request + job-status-polling state machine (ExportJobState sealed class), 7.2 wired up the actual download buttons and added a `dataReady` hybrid state.

Story 7.3's job: when a user requests an export over a date period with zero Entries, the UI must show its own terminal state ("Período vazio" — "Empty period") with no download action, explanatory copy suggesting the user adjust the period/filter, and no crash. This is reported via the backend's shared `{ code, message, retryable }` error shape with code `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`, which is non-retryable and must map onto the *existing* `Failure.exportEmptyPeriod` case (NOT a new Failure subtype).

I need a distilled investigation report (not full file dumps — just exact findings with file:line anchors) covering:

1. **Backend contract**: Open `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` and find the export endpoints (create export job, get export status, download). Specifically: is `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` returned as an error on the *create* call (i.e., the POST to create a job fails outright when the period has zero entries), or does it show up as part of the status-polling response (e.g. a `status` or `error` field on the job-status GET)? Quote the exact schema/field names and where this code appears. Also check `docs/input/backend/README.md` for the function-name mapping of these endpoints, and check `docs/input/backend/` for any error-taxonomy doc that defines `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`'s exact shape and whether it's retryable (confirm the retryable value matches what's already in lib/core/failure/failure.dart). Also check for a file like `export-screen-states.md` (referenced in a prior spec's Code Map) — read it fully if it exists, it may define exact state semantics/copy for the empty-period state.

2. **Prototype**: Check `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` and `docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html` for any "Período vazio" or empty-period export state — exact copy text (Portuguese), any icon/visual treatment, button/affordance (just "Fechar"?).

3. **Requirements doc**: Open `docs/input/requirements.md` and find Story 7.3's exact acceptance criteria text (search for "7.3", "Empty-Period", "Período vazio", "EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD").

4. **Current code** — read and report exact current shape (with line numbers) of:
   - `lib/core/failure/failure.dart` — confirm the `ExportEmptyPeriod` case, its `retryable` mapping, and `Failure.fromCode`'s `'EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD'` branch (already exists per a recent diff I saw — confirm exact current line numbers post-reformat).
   - `lib/features/export/domain/entities/export_job_state.dart` — full current sealed-class shape (all states, especially `preparing`, `generating`, `dataReady`, `done`, `error` if any).
   - `lib/features/export/data/models/export_job_status_dto.dart` — the `toState()` (or similar) mapping method, especially how it currently handles the create-call response and the status-poll response and whether/how it currently handles any error code at all.
   - `lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart` — how `_onExportTap`/create-job and polling currently handle a `Left(Failure)` from the repository (e.g. does create-job failure currently just show a SnackBar and leave sheet closed, or does it transition sheet state?).
   - `lib/features/export/presentation/widgets/export_status_sheet.dart` — the `_contentFor` state-dispatch structure (so I know where a new case would plug in) and current empty/error-state handling if any already exists.
   - `lib/features/export/domain/repositories/export_repository.dart` and its impl — the `createExportJob` (or equivalent) method signature, to see if it already returns `Either<Failure, T>` such that an empty-period failure would naturally flow through.
   - Any existing test file structure under `test/features/export/` relevant to error states (just note file paths, don't need full dumps).

Report back concisely: for each numbered area above, the key facts with file:line citations. Flag anything surprising (e.g. if EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD actually comes back from the status-poll endpoint rather than create, that changes the state-machine design significantly). Keep the report tight and factual — no implementation recommendations, just findings.

tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.

- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

9	## Stories
10	
11	- Story 7.1: Request a Period Export & Job Status Tracking
12	- Story 7.2: Narrative-Independent Raw-Data Download
13	- Story 7.3: Empty-Period Handling
14	
15	## Requirements & Constraints
16	
17	- Requesting an export is synchronous-on-enqueue: the create call returns a `jobId` and an initial `pending` status immediately; all progress after that is observed by polling a status endpoint (no push/streaming for export).
18	- The job's own `status` and the AI narrative's `narrativeStatus` are reported independently by the status endpoint, together with an entry count, per-leg error codes, and an explicit "download available" flag — the UI must branch on both fields together, never infer one from the other.
19	- Five user-visible states cover every combination: preparing (no download), generating summary (no download), a hybrid "data ready, summary still generating" state (raw download already enabled while narrative keeps processing underneath — this combination is not one of the five states shown in the prototype itself but is required by the live contract), done-with-summary (both PDF and raw download), and done-or-error-with-narrative-only-failure (raw download only, error copy framed around the narrative, never around the whole job).
20	- An export requested over a period with zero Entries surfaces as its own terminal state ("Período vazio") — no download offered, no crash — and the copy should suggest adjusting the period/filter rather than leaving a dead end.
21	- The narrative step uses a hosted AI model server-side; the app never calls it directly and never grades or asserts on the generated text's content.
22	- Downloading a finished artifact (PDF or raw) resolves through a redirect to a signed storage URL, not a direct JSON payload.
23	- Every export error still carries the shared `{ code, message, retryable }` shape; `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` is non-retryable, so it is never fed into generic retry handling.
24	
25	## Technical Decisions
26	
27	- Export lives in its own feature slice, following the same layer direction and `Either<Failure, T>` repository boundary used everywhere else; it introduces no new error-signaling shape.
28	- The closed, shared `Failure` hierarchy already carries a dedicated case for the empty-period error; export must map onto that existing case rather than defining a feature-local error type.
29	- The job's progress (pending → processing → data-ready/done/error, with narrative status layered on top) is its own small sealed state class, not forced into the shared single-fetch `idle/loading/data/error` resource pattern — this mirrors how other multi-stage async flows (capture processing, chat streaming) in this codebase already get their own state machine rather than reusing the generic one.
30	- Retry behavior for the underlying HTTP calls is not reimplemented per feature — the shared API client already retries the handful of server codes marked retryable, and export's status/download calls follow that same single retry path rather than adding a second one.
31	- Calls are made by function name, never the literal REST path: export's three operations (create job, poll status, download) each resolve to their own named endpoint, with the job id appended as a trailing path segment where required.
32	- Prefer one export surface with an internal status enum over separate routes per stage — the underlying job has five+ states but is one continuously-updating surface, not five screens.
33	
34	## UX & Interaction Patterns
35	
36	- Entry point is a download icon in the Meus Registros header; it opens a bottom sheet — the heaviest sheet surface in the product short of a full-screen modal — using the same rise-from-bottom entrance timing as other sheets (skipped under Reduce Motion, final state shown immediately instead).
37	- Each stage transition replaces the sheet's content in place; the sheet itself never closes and reopens mid-job, and every state keeps a "Fechar" dismiss affordance.
38	- State copy is plain and factual, never celebratory: preparing shows a spinner ("Preparando exportação..."); generating shows a progress bar ("Gerando resumo com IA..."); the hybrid state shows the raw-data download already enabled with summary-progress text still visible underneath; full success shows a confirmation plus both download actions (PDF primary, raw data secondary); a narrative-only failure keeps just the raw-data action with error copy scoped to the narrative; the empty-period state shows explanatory copy and a suggestion to adjust the period, with no download action at all.
39	- No swipe gestures and no nested overlays — the export sheet sits alone on the scrim over Meus Registros, never stacking on another sheet.
40	
41	## Cross-Story Dependencies
42	
43	- Story 7.1 establishes the export request + status-polling state machine; Stories 7.2 and 7.3 are both refinements of states that machine must already be able to represent (the data-ready hybrid state, and the empty-period terminal state), not independent flows.
44	- The epic depends on Meus Registros (Epic 4) already existing as the launch surface and as the source of the period/filter the export is requested over.

    16	  const factory Failure.authInvalid({required String message}) = AuthInvalid;

    36	  /// Local-only — the client's own parse-failure detection. `retryable` is
